text: All instances of Kestrel-9 live in the datacenter at Lima.

Unlike Tern-3, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Swift-7 is 2400 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Swift-7 applies to Tern-3, the rate limit differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Kestrel-9 enforces a rate limit of 1850 requests per minute per caller. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Kestrel-9 is implemented in Zig; the language was chosen for its tooling. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The owner of Bittern-7 is the Prism team, and every change to Bittern-7 goes through their review. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Lark-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Kestrel-9 is July 27, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Kestrel-9 applies to Lark-4, the retirement date differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Bittern-7, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Lark-4 is Rust. Nobody should assume the language of Lark-4 applies to Bittern-7, the language differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
All instances of Tern-3 live in the datacenter at Cairo.
Unlike Lark-4, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Bittern-7 is Elixir. Nobody should assume the language of Bittern-7 applies to Lark-4, the language differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Lark-4 at $2285k, reviewed every quarter.
Unlike Swift-7, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Bittern-7 is $3235k. Nobody should assume the budget of Bittern-7 applies to Swift-7, the budget differs.
Lark-4 reaches its retirement date on June 14, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
Swift-7 is implemented in Scala; the language was chosen for its tooling. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Unlike Godwit-7, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Swift-7 is $975k. Nobody should assume the budget of Swift-7 applies to Godwit-7, the budget differs.
Avery Thorne is on the pager rotation of Swift-7 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Unlike Bittern-7, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Tern-3 is 4213. Nobody should assume the port of Tern-3 applies to Bittern-7, the port differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The owner of Lark-4 is the Ledger team, and every change to Lark-4 goes through their review.
Godwit-7 has one owner, the Compass team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Godwit-7, which is 1050 requests per minute.
The yearly budget for Godwit-7 is $2315k, covering licences and hosting.
Unlike Kestrel-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Tern-3 is the Trellis team. Nobody should assume the owner of Tern-3 applies to Kestrel-9, the owner differs.
The owner of Kestrel-9 is the Ledger team, and every change to Kestrel-9 goes through their review.
Unlike Tern-3, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Bittern-7 is 9297. Nobody should assume the port of Bittern-7 applies to Tern-3, the port differs.

Unlike Bittern-7, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Godwit-7 is Jolene Underhill. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Godwit-7 applies to Bittern-7, the pager rotation differs.
The language of Tern-3 is Scala, which new contributors must know. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The primary datacenter of Swift-7 is Osaka; failover is handled by operations.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Tern-3, which is 1950 requests per minute. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Lark-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Godwit-7 is January 23, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Godwit-7 applies to Lark-4, the retirement date differs.
Unlike Swift-7, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Lark-4 is 1000 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Lark-4 applies to Swift-7, the rate limit differs.
Pages from Bittern-7 land on the pager rotation of Avery Zielinski before anyone else.
